first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the problem domain where memory_31 and memory_86 demonstrated durable gains. Both memories indicate signup/onboarding simplification drives activation and time-to-value. Verification of these two memories is critical before committing resources—we need to confirm the magnitude of lift and whether conditions remain similar. Memory_91 on activation messaging provides complementary support. This addresses root causes (completion decay) rather than masking them with pricing (memory_73 showed retention risk). Referral incentives (memory_57) target existing customers, not the current activation problem. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB activation decline. Promotional pricing directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue given memory_73's retention warning. A standard experiment on onboarding simplification is lowest-risk, highest-confidence path given inherited evidence.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories with strong evidence: exp_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with minimal retention risk (-1%); exp_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. Current situation shows 4% onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline QoQ. Simplified onboarding directly addresses both metrics. The verified results show durable gains without revenue quality harm, aligning with primary objective. SMB segment is being attacked by competitor pricing—onboarding simplification lifts their activation without triggering the retention collapse seen in memory_73 (promotional pricing). Memory_91 reinforces that product-side activation messaging compounds the effect. Standard experiment scale is appropriate: high confidence in direction, measured deployment, preserves ability to scale or pivot. No flagged downstream risks; retention data is positive.
